record.paper_title: The Future of Primordial Black Holes: Open Questions and Roadmap
record.original_question: Can PBHs make up most or all of the dark matter, particularly in the still-unconstrained asteroid-mass window around 10^-12 to 10^-16 solar masses, and what observations can constrain or identify PBHs in that window, including induced millihertz gravitational waves detectable by LISA, neutron-star capture and conversion to black holes in dense dark-matter environments, and stellar-mass-function suppression in ultra-faint dwarf galaxies?

evidence.quote: observational constraints eliminate this possibility for most of the range of possible PBH masses, with a notable exception around asteroid mass PBH, spanning several decades in mass around ∼ 10−12M⊙ down to the limit ∼ 10−16M⊙
The scenario of PBH as dark matter can be therefore tested in the future by LISA by measuring the GW two-point correlator.
It is of tantamount importance to come out with possible ideas for constraining or identifying PBH in the asteroid mass range.
One promising approach is that PBH capture leads to neutron star conversion to BH.
Another interesting avenue is to observe the number of massive main-sequence stars in ultra-faint dwarfs which should be suppressed if the dark matter is made of asteroid-mass PBHs

artifact.category_tag: primordial black holes as dark matter
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Primordial black holes (PBHs) are hypothetical black holes formed in the early universe from the gravitational collapse of large primordial density fluctuations, rather than from stellar collapse. Their cosmological abundance is conventionally parametrized by the fraction f_PBH = Ω_PBH/Ω_DM of the dark matter (DM) energy density made up by PBHs. Existing astrophysical and cosmological constraints (e.g. from microlensing, CMB accretion signatures, dynamical disruption of stellar systems, and Hawking-evaporation gamma-ray backgrounds) restrict f_PBH ≪ 1 over most of the PBH mass range, with the notable exception of the so-called asteroid-mass window M_PBH ∈ [10^{-16}, 10^{-12}] M_⊙, where currently f_PBH = 1 is allowed.

Address the following:

(a) Determine whether PBHs can constitute all (f_PBH = 1) or most of the dark matter when their mass spectrum is concentrated in the asteroid-mass window M_PBH ∈ [10^{-16}, 10^{-12}] M_⊙.

(b) Identify and quantitatively analyze observational probes capable of constraining or detecting PBHs in this window, including in particular:
   (i) the stochastic gravitational-wave background induced at second order by the scalar curvature perturbations responsible for PBH formation, with characteristic peak frequency in the millihertz band accessible to space-based interferometers such as LISA; compute the predicted GW two-point correlator (energy-density spectrum Ω_GW(f)) as a function of the primordial curvature power spectrum P_ζ(k) needed to produce the required PBH abundance, and assess the resulting detectability and constraints on f_PBH;
   (ii) capture of PBHs by neutron stars in regions of high dark-matter density (e.g. globular cluster cores, dwarf-galaxy centers) and the subsequent conversion of the host neutron star into a black hole, deriving the implied upper bound on f_PBH from the observed survival of old neutron stars as a function of M_PBH;
   (iii) suppression and modification of the low-mass end of the stellar mass function in ultra-faint dwarf galaxies due to dynamical heating and tidal disruption of star-forming regions by an asteroid-mass PBH dark-matter component, and the consequent constraint on f_PBH.

Provide a definitive, observationally validated answer to (a), or, failing that, sharp bounds on f_PBH(M_PBH) across the asteroid-mass window from each of the probes in (b).
artifact.status_search_result: The asteroid-mass PBH window (~10^-16 to 10^-12 M_⊙) remains observationally unconstrained as of 2024–2026, and whether PBHs constitute all the dark matter there is an open question. Recent reviews and forecasts continue to list this as an open problem, with LISA induced-GW measurements, neutron-star capture, and ultra-faint-dwarf stellar-population probes proposed as future tests but not yet decisive.

status_evidence.title: Primordial black holes as dark matter candidates (review)
status_evidence.snippet: The asteroid-mass window remains a viable region where PBHs could constitute all the dark matter; constraints in this range are weak.
status_evidence.claim: Asteroid-mass PBH dark matter remains observationally allowed.

status_evidence.title: The Future of Primordial Black Holes: Open Questions and Roadmap
status_evidence.snippet: Lists 'Are PBHs the Dark Matter?' as an open question, with the asteroid-mass window unconstrained and identifies LISA induced GWs, neutron-star capture, and ultra-faint dwarfs as future probes.
status_evidence.claim: Question is explicitly stated as open in a 2024 community roadmap.

status_evidence.title: Constraints on PBH from neutron star capture
status_evidence.snippet: Neutron star survival in dense DM environments places bounds on PBH abundance, but uncertainties in central DM densities of globular clusters limit the strength of these constraints.
status_evidence.claim: Neutron-star capture bounds on asteroid-mass PBHs are still uncertain.
